basis: Neuromuscular junction transmission disorder; myopathy occurs in 30-79%, with documented muscle fiber atrophy. Respiratory and ocular motor weakness reflect junction dysfunction.
Multiple exostoses and skull ossification defects define the skeletal disorder; developmental delay and intellectual disability are common. Eye movement signs do not establish intrinsic eye damage.
Disease directly involving tendons.
Defined by spastic paraplegia and Evans syndrome: autoimmune hemolytic anemia with autoimmune thrombocytopenia.
Mitochondrial/peroxisomal dysfunction causes encephalopathy; optic atrophy is frequent, with visual impairment and optic disc pallor in 3/4 patients.
Congenital remnants of the urachus, a urinary tract structure connecting the developing bladder and umbilicus. Infection is a possible complication.
Inherited frontotemporal neurodegeneration and/or motor neuron disease; dementia documented in 12/12 patients.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and heart malformations are very frequent; cleft palate/ectopic anus and microtia occur in 30-79%. Minor facial and eyelid dysmorphism adds no axis.
Inherited susceptibility specifically defined by CNS glioma; the label identifies the target organ, without implying an existing tumor or established damage.
Glioblastoma variant arising in the brain.
Progressive cerebellar degeneration with ataxia; abnormal pursuit, saccades and nystagmus reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than intrinsic eye damage.
OPA1-related optic atrophy causes visual loss. Extraocular manifestations affect a minority across the broad with-or-without phenotype; supplied ataxia frequency is 5-29%.
Autosomal dominant nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss.
Disease of pulmonary arteries with elevated vascular resistance; vessels and consequent right heart dysfunction fall within cardiovascular. Dyspnea does not establish lung tissue damage.
Acute malignant proliferation of T lymphoblasts in blood and marrow; leukemia alone does not establish an infectious or autoimmune mechanism.
Defined by cherubism/osteolysis, gingival fibromatosis and intellectual disability with seizures. Retinal pigmentation lacks documented functional damage; hirsutism alone adds no axis.
Childhood neoplasm directly occupying the brain stem.
Expansile skeletal osteolysis; conductive hearing loss in 16/20 from ossicular destruction; premature tooth loss affects most and is a defining manifestation.
Gastrin-secreting endocrine cell neoplasm arising in the pancreas or gastrointestinal wall. Peptic ulcer disease is separately diagnosed and is not added as involvement.
Adult oligodendroglial tumor arising in the central nervous system.
Congenital alopecia and hereditary palmoplantar keratoderma affect hair and skin.
Defined by hepatocellular retention of abnormal fibrinogen with variable liver injury and inherited hypofibrinogenemia, a coagulation disorder.
Tumor arises in the uterine corpus, a reproductive organ outside the axes. Uterine smooth muscle origin does not make it a skeletal musculoskeletal disease.
Antibody-mediated inflammatory demyelination defined by CNS disease and optic neuritis; optic nerve injury is ocular under these axes.
Focal epilepsy with preserved awareness, arising from abnormal cerebral electrical activity.
